IR.rationale: A rise in intermediate yields relative to the policy rate signals tighter expected US policy. That raises EM funding costs and tends to drive capital out of EM equities.

B.rationale: Widening Baa spreads together with weak high-yield returns mark tightening global credit conditions. Risky EM assets reprice in that state, possibly followed by a risk-premium rebound.

V.rationale: Elevated implied volatility and policy uncertainty together mark a fear state. The variance and uncertainty risk premia earned in such states predict higher subsequent risky-asset returns.

AP.rationale: Strong recent global equity returns tend to partially reverse at weekly to monthly horizons, and EM equities follow the US market with a lag.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms signals a flight to quality within equities. It reflects shifting risk appetite that carries over to EM risk premia.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength tightens dollar-denominated financing for EM borrowers and lowers dollar returns on EM assets. Sharp moves can also partly reverse.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity gains improve terms of trade and earnings in commodity-exporting emerging economies.

MC.rationale: Tight US financial conditions reduce global risk-bearing capacity and cross-border flows to EM, predicting weaker EM equity returns.

ENDG.rationale: Recent strong own returns can partially reverse at short horizons, or persist through momentum. The model learns which effect dominates.

IR.rationale: Abrupt repricing of US rate expectations is a recognised trigger of EM capital-flow reversals and of the turbulence that follows.

B.rationale: Credit deterioration, seen as widening spreads with falling high-yield prices, signals rising default and funding risk. That state leads equity volatility through the leverage and financial-accelerator channels.

V.rationale: Implied volatility contains forward-looking information about future variance beyond trailing realised variance, and global risk shocks spill over into EM.

AP.rationale: A joint sell-off in EM and US equities raises subsequent volatility through the leverage effect and volatility feedback.

ST.rationale: A rally in profitable, defensive stocks reflects flight-to-quality rotations that tend to accompany rising market turbulence.

FX.rationale: A strong dollar together with a weak risk-sensitive commodity currency marks global risk-off and dollar funding stress, which raise EM equity variance.

COM.rationale: Commodity sell-offs hit EM exporters' earnings and currencies and raise subsequent EM market variance.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions mean impaired intermediation and liquidity. That amplifies price moves and predicts higher future volatility.

ENDG.rationale: High recent variance relative to its own history captures the mean-reversion and clustering of volatility not fully explained by the baseline.

IR.rationale: A steepening driven by rising long yields reflects term-premium shocks that tighten global financing and pressure EM duration and equity valuations.

B.rationale: Widening corporate spreads together with falling EM sovereign bond prices signal EM-specific and global credit stress. This state often precedes sharp equity drawdowns.

V.rationale: Simultaneously elevated equity and gold implied volatility mark a broad cross-asset fear state, which fattens the left tail.

AP.rationale: Weak recent EM returns raise the chance of continued selling through flow-driven and leverage-driven feedback.

ST.rationale: Defensive quality outperformance signals de-risking by investors, which tends to coincide with downside episodes in riskier markets.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength tightens EM dollar-debt burdens and triggers capital outflows, raising crash risk in EM equities.

COM.rationale: Oil price slumps damage oil-exporting EM economies and signal weaker global demand.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions are a well-documented predictor of downside tail risk in growth and asset returns.

ENDG.rationale: An extreme recent own return reflects the current volatility regime and the potential for reversal, both of which shift tail probabilities.

IR.rationale: Falling expected US policy rates ease global financing and support strong rallies in EM assets.

B.rationale: Recent credit weakness raises risk premia, setting up the possibility of strong relief rallies.

V.rationale: High fear and uncertainty widen the return distribution and carry high risk premia, so large rebounds are more likely.

AP.rationale: Weak recent global equity returns tend to partially reverse, raising the odds of a strong subsequent EM gain.

ST.rationale: Flight-to-quality rotations mark stressed states in which the return distribution is wide, including in its right tail.

FX.rationale: Yen strength marks risk-off and carry-trade unwinding. It widens the distribution and precedes rebounds once positioning has been cleared.

COM.rationale: Commodity strength boosts EM exporters' earnings and currencies, supporting outsized EM equity gains.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress raises volatility and required returns, increasing the probability of large positive moves as stress eases.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent own returns raise valuations' upside potential and the likelihood of sharp short-term rebounds.
